spy.definition:
n. (military) a secret agent hired by a state to obtain information about its enemies or by a business to obtain industrial secrets from competitors
n. a secret watcher; someone who secretly watches other people
v. watch, observe, or inquire secretly
v. catch sight of; to perceive with the eyes
spy.translation:
n. 间谍, 侦探, 侦察
vt. 侦察, 找出, 发现
vi. 做密探, 侦查

spy on sb.translation: 暗中监视某人, 侦查某人

spy out.translation: [法] 秘密监视, 秘密侦察而发现

spy upon sb.translation: 暗中监视某人, 侦查某人

spy-hole.translation: n. 探视孔, 窥测孔

spy-holes.translation: (spy-hole 的复数) n. 探视孔, 窥测孔

spy-master.translation: [法] 间谍首脑, 特务头子

spyder.translation: n. 世爵（荷兰的汽车手工制造企业）；美国斯匹德（叉车及物流搬运设备制造商）

spygmogram.translation: [电] 记录动脉脉冲的运动, 型式和力量的图表

spyhole.definition: n a hole (in a door or an oven etc) through which you can peep

spyholes.definition:
plural of spyhole
n a hole (in a door or an oven etc) through which you can peep
spyholes.translation: (spyhole 的复数) n. 窥视孔

spying.definition:
n. keeping a secret or furtive watch
n. the act of keeping a secret watch for intelligence purposes

spymaster.definition: n. someone who directs clandestine intelligence activities

spymasters.translation: n. 间谍组织的首脑( spymaster的名词复数 )

spyware.definition: n. computer software that obtains information from a user's computer without the user's knowledge or consent
